title: Phase implementation plan document structure
description: Canonical structure of an osuperpowers phase implementation plan — the per-phase executable breakdown of one design spec. This schema is the single structure fact for the plan doc type: the header fields, the `### Task N:` colon-form task headings the brief extractor slices on, the per-task acceptance bullets, the Constraints source the dispatcher materializes plan-constraints.md from (canonical Form A literal `## Constraints` or legacy Form B prose pointers), the pending-acceptance-patch zone the orchestrator writes, and the `taskGroups` dispatch-group declaration the adjudication node writes (empty default ⇒ every task its own per-task group). Authoring agents read the properties + descriptions to draft conforming plans; docContractValidate / brief extraction consume the same patterns.

header.description: Plan header block — the first lines after the `# Title`; metadata fields, not `##` sections.

specRef.description: `**Spec:**` reference — the plan's approved design link, the same source as `plan-review`'s `--spec` pointer and report-issues' program attribution chain (plan record → `**Spec:**` → overall).

marker.description: The literal marker. Parsing semantics keep the engine contract (resolveSpecFromPlan): the marker is located by ANY-line findIndex — it may sit anywhere in the header. Line 2 (immediately after `# Title`) is the writing-plans template/example convention, NOT a schema required-position: a plan is valid wherever the `**Spec:**` line lives.

linkForm.description: Link form: `**Spec:** [<name>-design.md](docs/osuperpowers/specs/<name>-design.md)` — targets an existing spec file (repo-root form primary, file-relative fallback).

labelEqualsBasename.description: Class-A label rule — the link label must equal the resolved file's basename.

rule.description: `[<label>](<target>)` — the label must equal the basename of the resolved target (drift fails).

parentProgram.description: `**Parent program**` — link to the phase's parent overall (Class B lineage anchor).

linkForm.description: Link form: `- **Parent program**: [<name>-overall.md vX.Y](<path>)` — resolves to an existing `*-overall.md`, and the version tokens on the line must belong to the parent overall's lineage (its `**Version:**` header ∪ change-history cells).

version.description: `**Version**` — EXAMPLE field for a plan: only the phase-spec strictly requires a `**Version**` line; a plan header MAY carry one but no enforcing check reads it (the value has no lineage role at plan level). The example/template convention places it in the header block.

dependsOn.description: `**Depends on**` — upstream phase / spec pointers (e.g. `P1 design v1.1 Approved (sha)`); informational.

base.description: `**Base**` — the finishing read-base data source (e.g. `develop`); informational.

constraints.description: The plan's constraint surface — what `cdd implement` materializes plan-constraints.md from. Two declared sources (Form A or Form B); declaring neither is a plan-constraints-source-undeclared block (no silent fallback).

formACanonical.description: Form A (canonical, preferred): a literal top-level `## Constraints` section with the constraint body as `###` sub-sections under it.

heading.description: The literal `## Constraints` heading (the section is bounded by the next `##`/`#` heading, a `### Task` heading, or a `---` rule; `###` sub-sections stay inside).

formBProseAnchors.description: Form B (legacy): prose-pointer bold paragraphs in the preamble — the four canonical anchor names, each with a bold label + full-width colon.

items.description: One prose-anchor label token — bold name + full-width colon.

anchors.description: The four prose anchors (`口径` / `commit 边界机制` / `Flow Atomicity` / `顺序原则`), each a bold paragraph label followed by a full-width-colon block. A qualifier like `**commit 边界机制（本 program 全 phase 生效）**：` still occupies the anchor's slot; adding a suffix (`**commit 边界机制 补充**：`) makes it a different token and never fills the anchor requirement.

taskHeadings.description: Task headings — the brief extractor's slice surface (`/^### Task \d+:/`).

format.description: Colon format — `### Task N:` with an ASCII colon. A title after the colon is permitted and parse-tolerated (the extractor's slice surface `/^### Task \d+:/` ignores everything after the colon); only a non-`:` delimiter after the number (em dash, Chinese colon, bare space) fails brief extraction at dispatch time.

pattern.description: Task heading pattern — 1-indexed tasks from `### Task 1:` through `### Task N:`, an optional title after the colon is parse-tolerated.

continuity.description: Continuity rule — task numbers must be 1-indexed and contiguous (every number 1..max present exactly once; duplicates and gaps fail).

rule.description: extractTaskNumbers reads every `### Task N:` heading; the plan contract requires the extracted sequence to be exactly 1..N.

taskBlock.description: A per-task block under its `### Task N:` heading — the bullets the brief slices and the acceptance the plan carries.

do.description: `- **Do**:` — the do-brief for the task (what to implement).

acceptance.description: `- **验收**:` — the acceptance lines for the task; the brief extractor carries every acceptance line into the task brief verbatim, and the pending-acceptance-patch carry-through rides exactly this surface.

section.description: The `## Task Groups` section layout — the dispatch-group declaration's plan surface: the section heading const + the one-line entry form per merged group. Written to the plan ONLY when a non-trivial merged group exists (the write-back judgment: a length-1 group never lands on disk — the single-task state exists only as the empty default below).

heading.description: The section's top-level `##` heading (bounded like `## Constraints`: the next `#`/`##` heading, a `### Task N:` heading, or a `---` rule).

entry.description: One merged-group line — `- **Task 1, 2**: <note>` — the task numbers comma-space separated (the `--tasks <a>,<b>` join form).

items.description: One declared dispatch group — the plan record of a merged `--tasks <a>,<b>` dispatch. Declared only when 2+ tasks merge; a length-1 group is redundant (the single-group state exists only as the empty default).
One task number of the merged group (a `### Task N:` id).

tasks.description: The merged group's task numbers — unique and ascending (the deterministic group iteration order). minItems >= 2: a length-1 group is never declared.

taskGroups.description: Dispatch-group declaration — the orchestration record of the adjudication node (its sole writer), carried by the plan's `## Task Groups` section. Empty default: `[]` / an absent section ⇒ every `### Task N:` is its own singleton group — effectiveGroups = [[1],[2],…,[N]], exactly the pre-P4.3 per-task dispatch (zero migration); non-empty ⇒ the declared merged groups replace the singleton set entirely and the loop dispatches `--tasks <a>,<b>` per declared group. Section-persist rule: the section lands only when a non-trivial merged group exists — no groups → no section → empty default (zero plan churn).

pendingAcceptancePatch.description: Pending-acceptance-patch zone — a document convention, not a command-line contract: a top-level `##` section recording cross-task review findings tagged `targets later task` (task ref `### Task N:`, N later than the current task). The zone exists only while a patch is pending; the orchestrator is its sole writer (fix/implement agents hold zero plan-modification authority).

entry.description: One entry per pending patch: `- **Task N (patch)**: <task-ref + patch description>`.

carryThrough.description: Carry-through (mechanically assertable) — the later task's `- **验收**:` line carries the patch as an acceptance bullet, so the patch rides the standard brief-extraction surface (task headings + acceptance lines) into the later task's dispatch — no special parser, no schema change.

mechanism.description: The later task's acceptance bullet records `accepts pending-acceptance-patch (task-ref + patch description)`.

language.description: Repo authoring policy applies to the plan's prose — the plan at docs/osuperpowers/plans/ is an internal program doc written in the working language (Strategy B), value tokens (ids / tags / SHAs / paths) stay locale-neutral.
